newsitem.title: USA: Cascade enters Internet access business. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cascade enters Internet access business. [CORRECTED 14:55 GMT]

text.p: Cascade Communications Corp said Monday it plans to enter the Internet access equipment business by offering two new high-capacity dial-up Internet switches for use by telephone service carriers.
The company said it plans to begin offering in the fourth quarter (corrects time of offering) its AX 800 and AX 1600 High Capacity Access Switches.
The switches will provide the industry's highest capacity modem density in a single product and are designed to meet the rigorous requirements of service providers, Cascade said.
The AX switches integrate analog modem-based applications with high speed digital services, such as Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) and leased line Internet connections.
Cascade said its new offering will allow it to expand into new areas such as outsourcing of remote access and provision of multiple levels of service for Internet access.
The AX 800, aimed at applications that require mid-range capacity, is priced in the range of $27,500 to $200,000.
The AX 1600 is targeted for scalable high-end applications, and is priced in the range of $32,500 to $485,000.

"Now, for the first time, service providers can rapidly scale their dial-up networks to meet the explosive demand for access driven by the growth of the Internet and telecommuting applications," said Jim Dolce, vice president, remote access marketing, Cascade Communications Corp.
Scale refers to the capacity of the products to be expanded to handle thousands of simultaneous connections as demand for Internet access service increases.
"This is the same emphasis on scalability that made us a leader in the Frame Relay and ATM markets," Dolce said.
The executive was referring to Cascade's two existing core product lines switching produc lines, which are focused on the backbone portion of telecommunications networks.
Frame relay is a method of transmitting data at high-speeds and Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) allows voice video and data to be transmitted over backbone networks at high speeds.
